messages:
Samantha S (sales): FYI FinEdge POC can't reach the private endpoint in their VPC. Getting DNS failures and SSL errors. Can infra + SE swarm?
Alex (FinEdge): hitting an error when we curl the endpoint from our app subnet: 
```
curl -v https://private-inference.finedge.internal/v1/predict
*   Trying 10.10.5.21:443...\n* Connected to 10.10.5.21 (10.10.5.21) port 443 (#0)\n* ALPN, offering http/1.1\n* TLS error: SSL: certificate subject CN=redwood.internal doesn't match 'private-inference.finedge.internal'\n```
Response: curl exits and app fails TLS handshake.
Priya (se): thanks Alex. A few quick checks: 1) Are you resolving private-inference.finedge.internal to the interface endpoint IP (10.10.5.21)? 2) Is this an interface VPC endpoint (ENI) or a gateway? 3) Do you have split-horizon DNS or an internal zone pointing that hostname to the endpoint?
Alex (FinEdge): We have an internal hosted zone that points private-inference.finedge.internal -> 10.10.5.21. This works for other services. It's an interface endpoint (ENI).
Josh (infra): re: TLS error — it looks like the cert the endpoint is presenting has CN=redwood.internal and probably only internal SANs. Can you paste the full s_client output? In the meantime try: `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.21:443 -servername private-inference.finedge.internal` and check the certificate subject and SANs.
Alex (FinEdge): ran it, pasted snippet: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)\ndepth=2 C = US, O = Redwood Inc, CN = Redwood Root CA\ndepth=1 C = US, O = Redwood Inference, CN = Redwood Intermediate\nsubject=CN = redwood.internal\nX509v3 Subject Alternative Name:\n    DNS: redwood.internal, DNS: internal.redwood.cluster\n```
So no entry for private-inference.finedge.internal.
Priya (se): yep that's the issue — cert SANs don't include the customer's private hostname. For Private/VPC POCs we usually do one of: 1) Provide a cert with SANs that include the customer's internal hostname (requires CSR from the customer+approval), 2) Have the customer use the Redwood-provided internal DNS name (we map that to the endpoint IP), or 3) Terminate TLS at the customer's side and use a TLS pass-through. Which option did you plan?
Samantha S (sales): customer expected to use their hostname. They asked not to change app config. They prefer we add SAN. How long to get a cert change?
Josh (infra): timeline depends on certificate process and whether the customer's hostnames are in their private namespace (we need a CSR and proof of domain control for public names; for private internal names we can mint a cert signed by Redwood's internal CA but that requires configuring trust on the customer's side or bundling the CA cert). For a POC we can do a temporary workaround: add an entry in their app's /etc/hosts mapping the Redwood internal name to their expected hostname, or we can update the endpoint to present the Redwood hostname and ask client to set SNI to that name.
Alex (FinEdge): we cannot change app code or containers to add hosts file entries at scale. SNI change is also tricky (off-the-shelf client). Any alternative?
netbot (oncall): Also check firewall/security groups: interface endpoints require the endpoint's security group to allow inbound from the customer subnets on 443. If the ENI SG denies it you'll see connection resets rather than cert mismatches — but good to verify. Also make sure there are no strict egress NAT rules blocking access to ephemeral ports for the TLS handshake.
Priya (se): couple of pragmatic next steps for the POC swarming: 1) If FinEdge can accept installing our CA (we can provide it) into their app truststore for the POC, we'll mint a cert with the private hostname as SAN and rotate the endpoint cert — quick (few hours) once POA signed. 2) If they refuse, propose a network-level workaround: create an internal DNS alias `redwood-poc.finedge.internal` that we control, and we present cert for that name; then add a short-lived DNS CNAME in their internal zone pointing `private-inference.finedge.internal` -> `redwood-poc.finedge.internal`. That avoids app changes and keeps TLS intact.
Josh (infra): to implement option 1 we need: (a) CSR or hostname list from FinEdge, (b) confirmation they can add CA to truststore OR confirm that their runtime accepts our cert chain. Option 2 needs DNS TTLs low and agreement from their infra team to add the CNAME.
Samantha S (sales): Alex — can you ask your infra team which of these two they'd accept? Also they asked earlier about allowed IP ranges for the POC so they can open firewall egress. We have a small set of POC egress IPs for Dedicated trials: `34.198.12.45, 34.198.12.46`. Are those sufficient?
Alex (FinEdge): FinEdge infra wants exact list; they can open 443 outbound to those two IPs.
Priya (se): that should be fine for initial testing. Confirm security groups on our side also allow inbound from FinEdge's VPC CIDR to the interface endpoint SG. Josh, can you check our endpoint SG rules?
Josh (infra): checked — endpoint SG allows 0.0.0.0/0 on 443 (we tightened but left POC range open). However we do have a NACL on their side earlier that dropped some traffic; Alex, verify your subnet NACL allows ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for outbound.
Alex (FinEdge): confirmed NACL allows ephemeral outbound.
Priya (se): summary action items: 1) Alex to confirm whether FinEdge will install Redwood CA for POC or prefer DNS CNAME approach (Samantha to track sales ask). 2) Alex to temporarily allow egress to `34.198.12.45/46` so we can test. 3) Josh to prepare a temporary cert issuance path once CSR/hostnames are received. 4) Netbot to monitor logs for TLS SNI mismatches and share `deploy-bot` trace if failures continue.
Samantha S (sales): thanks all — I'll follow up with contract note about cert/CA for POC. Alex, if you can confirm today we should get a temporary cert and have them try again by EOD. :thumbsup:
Alex (FinEdge): OK sending CSR and internal contacts now. Appreciate the quick help. :eyes:
